questions.text: 21. Why is Beth unconvinced that allergies are linked to vitamin D deficiency?
options: A because people’s diets have improved since the 1950s
B because most people get enough vitamin D
C because the evidence only applies in Britain

correctAnswers.21: C because the evidence only applies in Britain

questions.instruction:
Questions 21–25
Choose the correct answer.
Climate change and allergies

questions.text: 22. Eliot explains that rising CO2 levels
options: A will mean distribution of pollen over a wider area.
B are having less impact on pollen than milder winters.
C are responsible for higher quantities of pollen.

correctAnswers.22: C are responsible for higher quantities of pollen.

questions.text: 23. What does Beth say about seasonal changes?
options: A There is no clear short-term trend for the arrival of spring.
B In general, spring is likely to continue arriving early.
C Springs are becoming milder and longer.

correctAnswers.23: A There is no clear short-term trend for the arrival of spring.

questions.text: 24. What point is made about the plant ragweed?
options: A it is spreading to more countries.
B it is the most widespread cause of allergies globally.
C it causes the most severe type of allergy.

correctAnswers.24: A it is spreading to more countries.

questions.text: 25. Why is tree pollen a more serious problem in cities?
options: A Trees produce more pollen there.
B There is less to absorb the tree pollen.
C There is not enough control over tree-planting.

correctAnswers.25: B There is less to absorb the tree pollen.

questions.text: 26. Question 26
options: A greatest change recorded for oak pollen
B changes identified for two pollen types only
C a longer season for grass pollen
D earlier start dates for all pollen types
E significant change in start date of birch pollen
F little difference in start dates

correctAnswers.26: G information only available for birch pollen
